name: Oak (Quercus robur), mature
notes: A mature pedunculate oak, LOW-POLY BUT FAITHFUL: every dimension is a real measurement and every material is catalogued, so the mass and centre of gravity DERIVE rather than being declared. Dimensions: 20 m tall with a crown as broad as it is tall and a bole up to ~1.5 m through (RHS/Missouri Botanical Garden; the species reaches 20-40 m in Europe). ★ THE CROWN IS A SPHERE OF FOLIAGE AT A DERIVED PACKING FRACTION, which is what `packing` exists for: a crown is overwhelmingly air. packing = LAI x leaf thickness / crown depth = 5.5 x 0.25 mm / 18.0 m = 7.64e-05. Both inputs are measured — temperate deciduous LAI ~5.5 m2/m2, deciduous woody lamina 0.25 +/- 0.08 mm — so the leaf mass is a consequence of the tree's size, not a number anyone picked. ★★ This is also what makes a canopy DARKER than its own leaves (docs/46 row 35) something the engine can eventually derive instead of declare: light entering a crown at this packing meets many leaves, and the mutual shadowing is geometry rather than a constant.
